html:
The Cochabamba Water War was a series of protests in the city of Cochabamba, Bolivia, from January to April 2000, against the sale of the city's water system to a private company.

Under pressure from the World Bank, the government had leased the water to a group led by the American firm Bechtel. Prices rose sharply, and a new law seemed to give the company rights even over wells and rainwater. Farmers, factory workers and townspeople joined in strikes and road blocks. The army was sent in and a teenager was shot dead.

In April the government gave in and the company left. The water war became a symbol worldwide of resistance to privatisation. In Bolivia it began the wave of protest that continued in the gas war and brought Evo Morales to power.
sum: The Cochabamba Water War was a series of protests in the city of Cochabamba, Bolivia, from January to April 2000, against the sale of the city's water system to a private company.
